Сәлем.Привет.Hello.

An attorney across borders, trained in Kazakhstan, the UK and the U.S.

I'm Gulnara. I'm licensed in Kazakhstan and have rights of audience at the AIFC Court, which works under English common law. I've practiced and taught law, and I now work on U.S. immigration cases, in Kazakh, Russian and English. It started in a village in Kazakhstan.

Before 2013

Kazakhstan

Village.

I grew up in a village in Kazakhstan. Every chapter below starts from there.

2013 – 2017

Almaty · Poland

Student.

I went to al-Farabi Kazakh National University on a state scholarship that covered four years of tuition. I joined the Femida law students' organization and took first place for leadership in 2014. I won international law conferences in 2015 and 2016. In 2016 I went to Adam Mickiewicz University in Poland on an exchange program, and in 2017 I graduated summa cum laude.

On the record
  • LL.B., al-Farabi Kazakh National University, Summa Cum Laude, 2017
  • State Merit Scholarship, full tuition, 2013 – 2017
  • 1st place, Leadership, "Femida" Law Students' Organization, 2014
  • Winner, International Law Conferences, 2015 – 2016
  • Exchange, Law & Administration, Adam Mickiewicz University, 2016

2017 – 2019

Gloucestershire · London

Scholar.

In 2017 I won the Bolashaq international scholarship for my LL.M. I started with a pre-masters program at INTO Gloucestershire University, then went on to University College London and finished my Master of Laws in 2019.

On the record
  • International Scholarship "Bolashaq" for LL.M. studies, 2017
  • Pre-Masters Academic Program, INTO Gloucestershire University, 2018
  • Master of Laws, University College London, 2019

2019 – 2021

Almaty

Trainee.

After London I went into practice at the bottom of the ladder. I was a trainee at Synergy Partners, then a legal assistant at Dentons in Almaty, then a barrister's trainee at Cicero Partners. I drafted motions and complaints, kept case files in order, did comparative research, and sat in on civil, criminal and regulatory hearings. I also kept clients and attorneys talking to each other, which is a bigger part of the job than it sounds.

On the record
  • Legal Trainee, Synergy Partners Law Firm, Dec 2019 – Mar 2020
  • Legal Assistant, Dentons, Almaty, Mar 2020 – Jan 2021
  • Barrister's Trainee, Cicero Partners Law Office, Apr 2021 – Feb 2022

2021 – 2022

Classroom · Bar

Teacher.

In 2021 I started teaching civil procedure and social security law at al-Farabi, in Kazakh, Russian and English. I led seminars on comparative legal systems and helped organize international conferences for the civil law department. Later I designed a Civil Procedure course at Narxoz University, with case-study modules and my own assessments. In February 2022 I became a licensed attorney.

On the record
  • Lecturer, al-Farabi Kazakh National University, Sep 2021 – Aug 2022
  • Senior Lecturer, Narxoz University, Sep 2022 – Jan 2023
  • Professional Excellence Diploma, Almaty City Bar Association, 2022
  • Cybersecurity & Human Rights training, SOROS Foundation, 2022
  • Trainer, Change Management & Innovative Teaching, Swiss-SASEM Academy, 2022

2022 – 2025

Almaty · Shymkent · Astana

Advocate.

For more than three years I represented clients in civil, criminal and administrative cases as a member of the Almaty City and Shymkent City Bars. I wrote case strategies, motions and affidavits, and I tracked the deadlines of many matters at once. In 2023 I gained rights of audience at the AIFC Court in Astana, which works under English common law. In 2024 I joined Shymkent Invest Company as counsel on corporate governance, labor issues and compliance.

On the record
  • Attorney, Almaty City & Shymkent City Bars, Feb 2022 – Aug 2025
  • Rights of Audience, Astana International Financial Centre Court, 2023 to present
  • Counsel, Shymkent Invest Company, May 2024 – Feb 2025

2025 – 2026

Connecticut

Newcomer.

I came to UConn Law for an LL.M. in U.S. Legal Studies. I worked at the law library and helped students and faculty find their way around Westlaw and Lexis. I mentored high school students in Hartford through the Lifting the Law program at the Boys & Girls Clubs. And I started working on U.S. immigration cases: asylum applications (I-589), employment-based green cards (I-140 NIW and I-485), work permits and removal defense.

I'm a member of AILA and the ABA, and I'm an associate editor for the ABA Young Lawyers Division.

On the record
  • LL.M. in U.S. Legal Studies, UConn Law, 2026
  • Library Assistant, UConn Law, Sep 2025 – May 2026
  • Mentor, "Lifting the Law," Boys & Girls Clubs of Hartford, Oct 2025 – Apr 2026
